analyst_view.overall: Castellón are 2nd with 30 points, unbeaten at Castalia, with the league's best defence (5 conceded in 13) and a 1-0 win at Valladolid last weekend; a win would put them top for at least three nights before leaders Almería play Ceuta on Monday. Eldense are 15th with 17 points after beating Sabadell 2-0, but have lost their last two away games and now lose captain and centre-back Jesús Clemente (dislocated shoulder) and Fidel Chaves (muscle problems), neither of which the numbers list; Guirao is back. Castellón are without Brignani (in the numbers) plus Fran Castillo, Rodrigo Rêgo and Isra Suero, a 6-goal midfielder who also missed the Valladolid win and is not in the numbers' list. Referee Pablo Morales Moreno (4.6 cards a game in 7) is already counted, and Javi Calleja promises a man-to-man press and no fear. The two sides' new absences roughly cancel out, so the view stays close to the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals, 2.0 of them Castellón's, with Brignani's injury already counted. Two absences the numbers don't know about pull in opposite directions: Castellón miss Isra Suero (6 goals in 686 minutes, though they won at Valladolid without him), while Eldense lose captain and centre-back Jesús Clemente to a dislocated shoulder. They roughly cancel, so I stay at 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, 5.7 of them Castellón's; they are one of the division's best possession sides at home and won 9 corners at Valladolid without Suero. Calleja says Eldense will press man-to-man rather than sit deep, which could cut a few home corners but also open the game, so nothing clearly points either way and I stay at 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards, with Eldense's heavy recent card count (20 in their last 6) and referee Pablo Morales Moreno's lower average (4.6 a game in 7, -5.4%) both already counted. Eldense's risky man-to-man press against a possession side can bring fouls, but that is how they have played all season, so I stay at 5.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.5 shots, 14.9 of them Castellón's. Castellón had 15 shots at Valladolid without Suero, and Eldense's press may give both sides chances, but with absences on both sides offsetting I stay at 24.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target. Castellón's defence allows very little and Eldense are without Fidel Chaves in attack, while Castellón miss Suero's finishing and Eldense lose Clemente at the back; these balance out, so I stay at 8.7.
